doc.title: Fred Radke interviewed by Monk Rowe, Hillsdale, Michigan, November 8, 2023

chapter: Lead trumpet and the rhythm section
title: Gregory Caputo quote and the Marine Band drummer at Wolf Trap
summary: A quote from drummer Greg Caputo and a Marine Band drummer's remark about Radke's reputation with drummers at the Wolf Trap anniversary.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: I have a quote for you from drummer Gregory Caputo, when he played with the Harry James band.

He said, “Fred having played with Harry James when Sonny Payne was playing the drums expected no less from me. I had to step-up my intensity and kick the band with the forcefulness of a Howitzer cannon.

Yeah. I’m famous for drummers. Well that’s what I’ve been told. When I was a guest soloist — one of the most important jobs I’ve ever done in my life — a guest soloist for the President’s own Marine Band, which was very important to me. And Jason — Colonel Fettig, who just retired by the way — invited me to do the Fiftieth Anniversary of Wolf Trap. And so I go in for the rehearsal in Washington and of course here’s the greatest musicians in the world sitting in this band. I said I’ve never seen so many Sergeant-Majors in my life in one place. And the drummer came up to me and he says, “I’ve been waiting for you.” I said, “What do you mean by that?” And he says, “Oh I’ve heard about you and drummers.” I said, “What have you heard?” And he says, “Well I’ve just heard some things.” And he was a great, just a great player. And he was with Andy Williams for years, he knew how to play.
